business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L561-1 et seq.) and Law n° 2017-399 of 27 March 2017 establishing the central register of beneficial owners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and shareholders against French, EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions and PEP lists using automated compliance tools

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of the French language in the Latin script; no transliteration required
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Generic business terms such as 'Société' or 'Entreprise' without specifying legal form; names that could mislead the public or infringe existing trademarks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, submit an administrative appeal to the President of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce within the prescribed deadline, typically 1 month

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SARL entities provided the registered office address is verifiable and functional for correspondence and administrative purposes
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; physical inspections are uncommon at the pre-incorporation stage and are conducted only in cases of suspected irregularities or during subsequent compliance reviews

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-Incorporation Legal Due Diligence and UBO Identification

Statutory consular legalization fees plus apostille costs
Official government tariff for name reservation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III: Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL formation, capital and management); L. 223-2 (no statutory minimum capital), L. 223-7 (full subscription; minimum one-fifth payment of cash shares), L. 123-11 and R. 123-30 et seq. (RCS registration); Loi Doubin, Article L. 330-3 C.com (franchise pre-contractual disclosure); Décret n° 2023-796 (Guichet Unique electronic formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; national electronic portal: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formulaires.entreprises.gouv.fr), coordinated by the Conseil National des Greffiers des Tribunaux de Commerce (CNGTC) / Infogreffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 'Demande d'immatriculation d'une personne morale au RCS' together with the executed Statuts (articles of association), submitted through the Guichet Unique; the incorporation is perfected upon entry in the RCS and evidenced by the official 'extrait Kbis'.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a SARL (L. 223-2 C.com); capital is freely fixed in the articles. At formation the capital must be fully subscribed and at least one-fifth (20%) of each cash share must be paid up (L. 223-7 C.com); in-kind contributions are fully released upon incorporation and the remaining quota may be called within five years. Cash contributions must be blocked on a dedicated escrow account ('compte bloqué de fonds') with a credit institution, a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the deposit attestation is filed with the RCS and the funds are released only upon production of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING ASSOCIATES OF [FR SARL BOBA TEA FRANCE]. The undersigned founding associates, acting as the initial corporate body, hereby resolve and agree: (1) the draft French Articles of Association are adopted; (2) each associate subscribes the shares shown in the subscription table, the capital being fully subscribed, and at least one-fifth thereof paid in cash as required by Article L. 223-7 of the Commercial Code; (3) the registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address] and statutory records are lodged there; (4) [Name] is appointed sole gérant for an indefinite term with full power to bind the company; and (5) the gérant is authorized to complete RCS registration, legal publication, and release of escrowed capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of French Articles of Association and Appointment of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding associates; notarial authentication is mandatory only when a real-property contribution is made, otherwise the Statuts may be executed under private signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the Statuts in French stating the corporate name, SARL form, registered office, duration, corporate purpose (franchise licensing of bubble-tea concepts; manufacture and supply of syrups, toppings and packaging), share capital, share subscription table and powers of the gérant. Verify the corporate name is not pre-empted through the RCS/INPI databases. Each associate must subscribe his or her shares and pay at least 20% of the nominal cash amount; if a contribution in kind (e.g., equipment lease, trademark licence, existing stock) is made, such contribution must be fully delivered at incorporation and described in an annex. Collect declarations of non-conviction of the future gérant.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts with object clause covering franchise licensing and syrup supply chain activities
Valid passport or national identity document of each associate and the proposed gérant
Declaration of non-conviction (bulletin n°3 extract or sworn declaration of eligibility to manage)
Evidence of lawful enjoyment of the registered office (lease, bail commercial, or ownership deed)
In-kind contribution valuation report if applicable (commissaire aux apports)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or notary queries any statutory clause, convene an extraordinary general meeting of associates to amend the affected article; re-sign and, where applicable, re-authenticate the corrected pages; file the corrective resolution with the Guichet Unique within 8 days and, failing that, respond to any Greffe 'injonction de régulariser' within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocking of the Share Capital on an Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution approved by the Banque de France, a notarial escrow account, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked capital account in the name of the company to be formed. Pay into it at least one-fifth of the cash subscription of each share. Obtain the 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' or 'certificat de consignation' issued by the depositary institution. The funds remain frozen until presentation of the RCS registration certificate (Kbis) and a release instruction from the gérant. If the capital is partly composed of in-kind contributions, no cash is due for that portion, but the contribution must be evidenced by the annex to the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Copy of the signed Statuts and share subscription table
Power of attorney or authority letter of the person opening the escrow account
Identity documents of the associates and beneficial owner declaration (AML/KYC)
Bank account instructions and payment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the bank delay the attestation for AML/KYC checks, complete enhanced due diligence and obtain an updated certificate; alternatively transfer the funds to a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations within 5 working days; request a re-issued attestation quoting the exact corporate name, capital amount and intended RCS office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Statutory Formation Notice in a Legal Announcements Journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A journal authorized to receive legal announcements (JAL) in the department of the registered office, selected from the prefecture-approved list.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the 'avis de constitution' containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, the RCS city of registry and the identity of the gérant. Submit the notice to the chosen JAL, pay the publication fee, and obtain the 'attestation de parution'. The statutory period requires publication before or simultaneously with the RCS application; the attestation is annexed to the M0 filing. For franchise networks, no separate JAL publication is required for the Loi Doubin disclosure, which is contractual only.
required_dossiers: Text of the formation notice (avis de constitution)
Extract or full copy of the signed Statuts
Power of attorney if publication is filed by counsel
Payment voucher for the insertion fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains typographical or legal inaccuracies, publish a correcting notice (avis rectificatif) in the same JAL stating the exact corrected particulars and transmit the correcting attestation to the Greffe; ensure the corrected notice is inserted before the RCS examination deadline of 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the RCS via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formulaires.entreprises.gouv.fr), routed to the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce competent for the registered office; the Greffe issues the récépissé and performs the legal compliance check.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 application for the registration of a legal entity in the RCS. Upload the executed Statuts, the bank/escrow deposit attestation, the JAL publication attestation, proof of the registered office address, identity and eligibility documents of the associates and gérant, and the beneficial ownership declaration. Pay the statutory greffe fee online. The Greffe verifies the corporate name availability, the legality of the purpose, the capital rules and the capacity of the gérant; upon acceptance it records the company in the RCS and transmits the data to INSEE and DGFiP.
required_dossiers: M0 electronic declaration duly completed
Signed Statuts in a single consolidated PDF, initialed by each associate
Attestation of deposit of funds issued by the bank, notary or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
Attestation of the JAL publication of the formation notice
Proof of lawful occupation of the registered office (lease, rent receipt or ownership deed)
Identity documents and declaration of non-conviction of each associate and the gérant
Beneficial ownership declaration (document for the RCS register of beneficial owners)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a rejection or a 15-day 'injonction de régulariser', cure the filing by uploading the missing annexes through the Guichet Unique within the prescribed delay; request a provisional registration (immatriculation provisoire) where only minor points are outstanding; appeal a definitive refusal before the Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Kbis Extract, French Company Numbers and VAT Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce (Kbis extract); INSEE (SIREN/SIRET and APE/NAF activity code); DGFiP (French intra-community VAT number).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Greffe issues the 'extrait Kbis', which is the exclusive proof of legal existence of the SARL. INSEE automatically assigns the SIREN, the SIRET establishment number, and the APE code corresponding to the principal activity; a tea-based beverage service and franchise holding activity will normally receive APE 5610A (restauration traditionnelle) or, where licensing predominates, APE 7022Z. DGFiP allocates the FR intra-community VAT number through the same Guichet Unique notification. Verify all identifiers on the Kbis and retrieve the SIREN/SIRET record from the public INSEE/Annuaire des Entreprises database.
required_dossiers: RCS registration receipt or electronic confirmation of immatriculation
Kbis extract request via the Greffe or online download from infogreffe.fr
INSEE allocation notification of SIREN/SIRET/APE
DGFiP VAT certificate if required for intra-community franchise supplies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains divergent particulars (capital, registered office, gérant), file an online modification form through the Guichet Unique and request a 'certificat de mise à jour' with an issue within 10 days; for INSEE coding disputes, contest the APE attribution before the INSEE business register helpdesk; for VAT errors, file form 1447C with the local business tax office (SIE).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Health Registration, HACCP Compliance and Franchise Disclosure (Loi Doubin)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP/DDETSPP) for food establishment registration and sanitary inspection; DGCCRF for commercial and franchise practice control; no filing is required for the Loi Doubin information document but its service is mandatory before signing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'déclaration d'ouverture' of the food preparation and beverage-serving establishment under Article L. 233-2 of the Rural and Maritime Fishing Code and Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Annex II. Attach the Plan de Maîtrise Sanitaire (PMS) covering HACCP, allergen management, syrup pasteurization, cold chain, cleaning and staff hygiene; a 14-hour food hygiene training certificate for the manager is required. If syrups and concentrates are supplied to franchisees, the unit remains a 'déclaré' establishment because the products are of non-animal origin. Before executing any franchise agreement, serve the prospective franchisee with the 'Document d'Information Précontractuelle' (DIP) at least 20 days prior to signing, containing truthful financial and network data, in accordance with Loi Doubin.
required_dossiers: DDPP food establishment opening declaration (CERFA sanitary form)
Plan de Maîtrise Sanitaire (PMS) including HACCP, allergen and traceability procedures
Kbis extract and SIRET number of the SARL
Food hygiene training certificate (14-hour module) of the responsible manager
Floor plan of the kitchen, syrup workshop and public sales area with equipment list
Water supply and wastewater evacuation certificate issued by the sanitation authority
Loi Doubin DIP dossier with 20-day service proof and franchisor annual accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DDPP sanitary inspection records non-conformities, submit a corrective action plan within 30 days and provide evidence of implementation; in case of suspension or closure order, appeal before the Tribunal administratif in summary proceedings; if a franchisee quibbles the DIP content, issue a complete replacement DIP before signature and document the resumption of the 20-day cooling-off period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP / DDETSPP per department) for food-business registration and sanitary control; Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for any ICPE environmental registration; DGCCRF for commercial, pricing and franchise practice supervision.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'ouverture d'un établissement de préparation et de vente de boissons (restauration commerciale) under Article L. 233-2 du Code rural et de la pêche maritime and Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, supplemented by the Loi Doubin franchise disclosure obligation under Article L. 330-3 du Code de commerce.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), ICPE and non-domestic wastewater units, in coordination with the Agence Régionale de Santé (ARS) for water and food safety aspects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report not required. The operation is an ICPE-exempt or 'Déclaration' regime unit under Rubrique 2781 (food processing/preparation) only where the syrups workshop exceeds 12 tonnes of prepared food per day; a standard bubble-tea franchise kitchen and syrup mixing room falls below the threshold and is therefore exempt from ICPE, requiring only the DDPP sanitary declaration and, where applicable, a prefectural declaration for non-domestic wastewater discharges exceeding 15 m³/day or 30 kg BOD5/day.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: connection to the municipal sewerage system under the communal sanitation regulation; mandatory grease interceptor (minimum 750 L) on the kitchen and syrup-line effluent; typical compliance limits for any non-domestic discharge: pH 6.0–8.5, temperature ≤ 30°C, COD ≤ 2 000 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 800 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 600 mg/L, mineral oils and fats ≤ 100 mg/L. Fugitive emissions: cooking and tea-condiment odors captured by extraction hoods fitted with activated carbon filters; VOC concentration at the discharge stack ≤ 50 mg/m³ (below the threshold of the arrêté of 2 February 1998, hence no abatement authorization required). Waste: used cooking oils and boba residues removed by an authorized collector with a waste tracking slip (bordereau de suivi de déchets); recyclable packaging and biodegradable waste sorted per municipal scheme; any waste stored under cover to prevent leachate infiltration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: 5th-category ERP (N ≤ 200) clearance by the Commission de Sécurité, including ventilation, emergency exits, fire extinguishers and a kitchen fire-suppression system. Structural: technical control by a certified bureau de contrôle (e.g., SOCOTEC, APAVE) for floor load capacity of the syrup storage area and any mezzanine seating, and verification of the grease-extraction duct. Occupational: affiliation to the statutory occupational health service (médecine du travail), completion of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), electrical installation conformity certificate for kitchen equipment, posting of mandatory notices, and the 4-yearly medical aptitude review for the staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: France – Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Public Accounts; tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; business formalities one-stop: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs authority for export procedures: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – DELTA platform; public e-invoicing hub: Portail Public de Facturation (PPF).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the SARL via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (art. R.123-9 Code de commerce); INSEE automatically assigns SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits) with APE/NAF 5610A/5610B. (2) DGFiP registers the entity ex officio for Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) and allocates the TVA intracommunautaire number (FR + 2-digit key + SIREN), verifiable in the EU VIES database. (3) Non-resident ownership is permitted without minimum capital requirement (SARL capital freely set). (4) For goods export, the SARL obtains an EORI number (FR + SIREN) activated with DGDDI for lodging the DAU export declaration. (5) A French-established SARL is a French tax resident by operation of law; no separate foreign-entity registration procedure is needed, but transactions with non-resident shareholders trigger transfer-pricing and anti-hybrid documentation obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – SARL is taxable on its own account under art. 206-1 CGI at the flat 25% IS rate on profits attributable to French business operations (territorial scope under art. 209 CGI; foreign PE profits excluded with foreign tax credit). No pass-through to members; distributed dividends are subject to the 30% flat withholding (PFU) or the 12.8% option, plus 3% social contribution on distributions. The entity cannot elect any check-the-box flow-through status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box or elective hybrid classification. Express legal elections available: (i) option for income-tax regime (art. 239 bis AA CGI) for SARLs with a maximum of 50 individual shareholders and corporate capital not exceeding 10%, irrevocable for five accounting periods; (ii) fiscal integration (art. 223 A CGI) for a chain of at least 95%-owned French subsidiaries headed by an IS parent; (iii) VAT filing simplification (régime réel simplifié, art. 293 CC CGI); (iv) interest deduction cap and anti-hybrid rules (art. 212 bis CGI implementing ATAD) apply mandatorily – no elective carve-out; an EBITDA-based 30%/EUR 3 million limitation is the default statutory ceiling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; arts. 256 to 283 nonies CGI)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise-en-base thresholds in force for 2025: EUR 91,900 annual turnover for supplies of goods; EUR 36,800 for services (franchise royalty income falls in the services category); tolerance ceilings EUR 101,000 and EUR 39,100. The SARL exceeds the EUR 36,800 services threshold in its first fiscal year by the nature of the franchise model (royalties plus syrup supply), so TVA registration is compulsory from the first taxable transaction without any de minimis suspension; the EUR 10,000 EU distance-sales threshold only concerns non-established EU sellers and is not relevant to this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing under art. 289 CGI and ordonnance n° 2021-1190, as deferred by décret n° 2023-888: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices, and large enterprises (≥ EUR 150M turnover / 500 employees) and mid-sized enterprises must issue e-invoices; small and medium enterprises must issue e-invoices from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be transmitted through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) in Factur-X, UBL or CII formats; e-reporting of domestic sales within 1 business day and of intra-EU/export transactions within 10 days is transmitted to DGFiP. France does not apply per-invoice fiscal stamping or real-time pre-approval by the tax authority; compliance is enforced by ex-post analytics on PPF data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération avec droit à déduction) applies under art. 262-I-1° CGI to goods definitively exported from the EU customs territory; the French SARL must prove physical exit of the goods using the DGDDI electronic export procedure (DAU accepted and MRN closed by customs, with exit within the customs-prescribed deadlines – presentation generally within 30 days and exit monitored under UCC art. 107). Syrups and supplies shipped to foreign franchise outlets qualify; prepared beverages sold by French domestic franchisees remain taxable in France (10% reduced rate for drink service) while franchise royalties invoiced to foreign franchisees are B2B services placed outside France under arts. 259-259 C CGI (destination principle, reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction) and must carry the mention 'TVA non applicable – art. 259 B CGI'. No statutory French FX-repatriation deadline exists for VAT zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is an internal treasury/customs audit reference (cross-border cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more are reportable under the Code monétaire et financier).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) lodged in the DGDDI DELTA platform with MRN closure
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR consignment note (road) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoice stating the export nature, the SARL's TVA intracommunautaire number and the foreign franchisee's VAT/identification number
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing payment by the foreign franchisee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and DGDDI cross-match the DAU/MRN data, transport documents and PPF e-reporting; failure to substantiate export triggers reversal of the zero-rating with re-invoicing of 20% VAT, monthly late interest of 0.20% (art. 1727 CGI) and penalties of 40% for bad faith or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (art. 1729 CGI); fictitious or non-compliant invoices expose the issuer to a 50% amende (art. 1737 CGI); tax fraud (art. 1741 CGI) may entail criminal fines up to EUR 500,000 and seven years' imprisonment for the gérant, with joint and several liability under art. L.267 LPF; clawback of input VAT improperly deducted is retroactive. The statutory reassessment window is three years for declared operations and six years for undeclared ones (art. L.176 LPF), with a ten-year customs penalty horizon.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks, jointly with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as the prudential supervisor, the Direction Générale du Trésor of the French Ministry of Economy and Finance for foreign-exchange authorizations relating to non-cooperative states, and TRACFIN as the French Financial Intelligence Unit. The legal basis is the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), in particular Articles L151-1 et seq. CMF and Décret n° 89-938 du 29 décembre 1989 on financial relations with foreign countries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies unrestricted euro convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior French exchange-control approval is required for ordinary inbound equity injections, franchise royalty collections, intercompany loans, or profit remittances to non-resident shareholders. Residual constraints are limited to EU/UN economic sanctions, the French non-cooperative states (ECNC) regime requiring prior ministerial authorization for certain financial relationships, and the enhanced documentary and beneficial-ownership reporting imposed by French AML/CFT law. Dividends and royalties may be repatriated freely, provided the remitting French bank receives a valid purpose code and the transaction, where applicable, is captured in the Banque de France balance-of-payments and annual liaison financière returns. Related-party remittances must be supported by transfer-pricing substance documentation to withstand both tax and AML characterization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has abolished general export-proceeds surrender and forced-conversion rules. Under the current liberalized framework, export receipts from ordinary jurisdictions may be retained in foreign currency, and no statutory percentage conversion into euros and no statutory repatriation deadline apply. The SARL is expected only to book the proceeds in its accounting records and to allow the collecting French bank to perform the required statistical declaration to the Banque de France. Exceptional mandatory repatriation and euro conversion may be triggered solely for transactions involving countries on the French ECNC list or designated jurisdictions under EU/UN sanctions, in which case prior authorization from the Direction Générale du Trésor is required, and full repatriation through a licensed French credit institution with conversion of the proceeds must be completed within the contractual settlement period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué pour libération du capital) / Operational Account (compte courant professionnel)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. (Groupe BPCE – Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for auxiliary multi-currency treasury operations, but not acceptable as the sole banking relationship. ACPR-regulated French electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto S.A., Shine S.A. (Groupe Société Générale), and MangoPay S.A. may provide French IBANs, virtual IBANs, SEPA and SWIFT collections, and multi-currency e-money wallets. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot grant credit, receive deposits, or pay interest on balances, and their e-money balances are not covered by the French deposit guarantee (FGDR); EMIs typically refuse SWIFT beneficiary credits from high-risk, sanctioned, or formally restricted foreign jurisdictions; currency conversion must be executed by a licensed payment institution or credit institution rather than the EMI itself; derivatives and structured FX hedging cannot be delivered through the EMI platform. For the global franchise royalty network, the EMI is best used as a treasury dashboard and SEPA collection gateway, whilst the legal settlement backbone must remain a tier-1 French bank holding the capital account and executing hedging documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 French commercial banks normally require an in-person KYC interview at a branch for the statutory gérant and for each direct or indirect shareholder holding 25% or more of the SARL. Remote video identification is legally available under Article R561-5 CMF and has been used for EU/EEA-resident individuals, but for non-EEA corporate shareholders and their ultimate beneficial owners, banks consistently demand physically certified passports, apostilled corporate registry extracts, French notarized translations of constitutive documents, and either a personal interview with the local branch or an acceptable interview conducted by a foreign correspondent bank on behalf of the French credit institution. A French registered office, a valid Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing, and a French tax representation are compulsory. For the target business profile, onboarding is achievable at BNP Paribas and Société Générale within a 4–8 week timeline if the shareholder’s home country documentation is professionally apostilled and the economic purpose of the French SARL is clearly documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A non-resident corporate shareholder domiciled in a common-law or offshore-adjacent jurisdiction (Hong Kong, Singapore, UAE) with a multi-layer ownership chain; French bank compliance may classify the file as opaque ultimate-beneficial-ownership and default to refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and Memorandum and Articles of Association apostilled and translated into French; up-to-date corporate register extract showing directors and shareholders; signed ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration with passport copies; a group organization chart covering each ownership layer; a bank reference letter issued within the last 3 months by the shareholder’s principal bank; source-of-wealth documentation (audited financial statements, tax returns, or asset sale deeds) supporting the subscription amount; and a board minute of the shareholder approving the French capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent inbound royalty wires from overseas franchisees labelled as 'trade fees' in different Euro amounts; the receiving bank may suspect the SARL is operating as an unlicensed payment institution or is commingling third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master franchise agreement and each underlying franchisee licence; published franchise fee schedule and royalty calculation methodology (percentage of gross sales); monthly royalty invoices (factures) issued by the SARL to each franchisee; a sample SWIFT MT103 per inbound wire showing the purpose code 'ROYL' (royalties and licence fees); accounting ledger extracts demonstrating that only the SARL’s own revenues are collected, with no pass-through or client money; and the Banque de France statistical declarations when reportable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Procurement of boba tea syrups, tapioca pearls, packaging, and equipment from non-EEA suppliers in China, Taiwan, Thailand, or Vietnam; the French bank may reject payment because the supplier’s jurisdiction is greylisted by FATF, sanctioned, or subject to enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoice, packing list, transport documents (B/L, AWB, CMR) and Incoterms 2020 clause; French customs import declaration (DAU) and underlying export customs documents; supplier certificate of origin and a shipping-route attestation proving no transit through sanctioned territory; completed EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening reports for both the supplier and the receiving bank; the signed supply contract containing an arbitration clause; and documentary evidence of import VAT and duty payments in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A rapid inbound shareholder loan (compte courant d'associé) followed by early repayment or profit distribution; this pattern may trigger an Article L561-1 et seq. CMF declaration for money laundering, tax concealment, or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly signed and registered shareholder loan agreement (convention de compte courant d'associé) with arm's-length interest terms and repayment schedule; corporate authorisations of both the SARL and the lending shareholder; complete bank and ownership trail from the original source of funds to the French account; statutory financial statements and the profit appropriation (affectation du résultat) minutes; French transfer-pricing documentation under Articles L13 AA and L13 AB of the French Tax Procedure Code; and evidence that the funds were used for identifiable operational expenses of the franchise network.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital injection protocol: (1) The SARL opens a dedicated capital escrow/subscription account (compte bloqué) at BNP Paribas or Société Générale and obtains the bank’s commitment to release funds upon registration; (2) the non-resident shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 (from a non-EEA jurisdiction) or SEPA Credit Transfer (from an EEA jurisdiction) strictly in EUR, naming the SARL as beneficiary with full legal name and registration number; (3) the payment must contain in Field 70 the remittance information referencing the deed of subscription (bordereau de souscription), the file reference of the French notary or bank, and the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity capital) or 'INVL' (investment loan) for shareholder advances; (4) the French bank will verify the deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued under the French Commercial Code and will ensure the balance-of-payments declaration is transmitted to the Banque de France where the transaction threshold applies; (5) after publication of the incorporation notice, the funds are released into the SARL’s operational account. For remittances originally in USD, RMB, or HKD, the shareholder’s bank must convert the amount into EUR before transmission and state the all-in EUR value in the SWIFT instruction to avoid residual shortfall.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) SWIFT MT103 Customer Credit Transfers for non-EEA suppliers, international logistics providers, and overseas franchise support, sent through the French bank’s EUR clearing on TARGET2 or through its USD correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire) for USD-denominated contracts; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfers and SEPA Instant Credit Transfers for recurring EEA suppliers of syrup concentrates, packaging, and European sub-franchisees; (iii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (sight or usance) issued on the SARL’s account under ICC UCP 600 and pre-advised via MT700 by the issuing French bank for large-volume purchases of tapioca, tea leaves, and equipment from Asia; (iv) Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98 or on-demand bank guarantees where the SARL provides security to franchisees or suppliers; (v) Documentary Collections (CAD/DP) for mid-sized non-EEA batches. All non-EUR disbursements above EUR 50,000 must be covered by a confirmed FX deal and the underlying commercial invoice; payments to ECNC-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions must be pre-cleared by compliance; French customs export declarations (DAU/EXA) and certificates of origin must accompany goods-related settlement documents to satisfy Banque de France statistical requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) limited to demonstrable commercial exposure arising from franchise royalties, syrup imports, and intercompany flows, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement with acceptable CSA collateral terms.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid Asian currencies (CNY, MYR, VND, TWD, KRW) executed through an ACPR-authorized credit institution or an international market-maker, strictly for hedging underlying trade or royalty inflows, with a maximum maturity of 12 months and no leverage.

Cross-currency swaps (vanilla fixed-for-fixed or floating-for-floating) to align the currency denomination of the SARL’s intercompany shareholder debt and the future royalty stream in EUR, USD, and RMB, subject to French bank credit approval and prudential documentation.

European-style FX options (protective puts, zero-cost collars, risk reversals) for the purchase price of imported goods and forecast royalty receipts; writing uncovered options or entering exotic/leveraged derivatives is unavailable to a non-professional corporate client under MIFID II and would be rejected by French compliance as an unhedged speculative transaction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual financial statements, management report (if required), and accompanying statutory audit report, filed with the Commercial Registry (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) / INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; shareholders' ordinary meeting must approve accounts within six months of fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, approval is due no later than 30 June and filing typically by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal injunction to file, fines of up to EUR 9,000 for non-compliance by legal representatives, and failure to file for two consecutive financial years can trigger proceedings seeking judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and annexes (liasse fiscale: form 2065-SD and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) via EDI-TDFC electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due by 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends, within three months of the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 5% of the tax due, increased to 10% after 30 days, plus monthly late interest of 0.20%; omission penalties of EUR 150 per missing schedule; continued non-filing can trigger upward reassessment of taxable base.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration of effective beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filed or updated upon changes; annual consistency review performed at the annual shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) / INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any transfer of quotas/shares or change in beneficial ownership or control; no annual filing is required when such data remain unchanged. Annual involuntary checking is part of the ordinary meeting formalities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 and imprisonment up to six months for intentional omission or false beneficial-owner information; risk of administrative strike-off and temporary exclusion from public procurement procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax declaration and payment (Contribution Foncière des Entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - competent SIE or Centre des Finances Publiques
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on 15 December of the current tax year (next business day if the 15th falls on a weekend); assessed on prior-year property net rental values.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment uplift of 10%, monthly late interest, and possible reassessment of under-declared rental values, including penalty interest and additional fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the end of a financial year, the entity exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. The franchise royalty and syrups supply model will trigger audit if the entity belongs to a consolidated group meeting separate conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (PCG), anchored by ANC Regulation 2014-03 and articles L.123-12 to L.123-22 of the Code de commerce; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted only for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France mandates a public beneficial-owner declaration at incorporation and an event-driven update within 30 days of any transfer of quotas, change of beneficial ownership, or modification of voting control. There is no standalone annual UBO filing; instead, the SARL must review the declaration during its ordinary annual general meeting and file an update if any event has occurred. A share transfer in the franchising chain will therefore require a parallel RCS beneficial-owner amendment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of quota holders and members (registre des associés et des mouvements de titres)
Register of shareholders' decisions and minutes of general meetings (registre des décisions d'associés)
Register of attendance sheets for physical meetings and written consultation records
Register of quota transfers and capital movements (registre des cessions de parts)
Minute book of manager's decisions within delegated powers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $450 - $1,450 per year for licensed registered-office and corporate agent services in French business centres
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,200 - $13,500 for a typical small SARL audit engagement; not mandatory below the statutory auditor thresholds unless voluntarily appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; prior fiscal years: 26.5% to 27.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate applicable to small and medium enterprises on taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 per 12-month period; patent box regime taxes income from qualifying IP at 10%; research tax credit (CIR) of 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; innovation tax credit (CII) of 20% of certain prototype design expenditure.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no legal expiry; annual utilisation cap EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profits under Article 209 CGI)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return (liassez fiscale): Form 2065-SD plus annexes 2058-SD to 2058-FE-2 and 2065-bis-SD, electronically filed through the EDI/EFI portal of impots.gouv.fr (mandatory for SARLs unless a French micro-entity exception applies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with four prepayment instalments: 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and a balancing payment due with the annual return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closing on 31 December, no later than the second business day after 1 May. For any other year-end, within three months after the closing date. The balancing payment is due at the same time as the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: SIREN, SIRET, legal form (Société à Responsabilité Limitée), APE/NAF code corresponding to ISIC 5610 restaurant and franchise activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity with a French branch or PE must report French registered office details and no foreign address; for an SARL, tax residence is France; if PE status is contested, attach treaty analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: date of opening and closing, duration not exceeding 12 months except first period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French fiscal year adopted in the bylaws; should align with franchise reporting year for royalties and supply-chain transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal – bénéfice (taxable result): net accounting profit before tax, after statutory depreciation and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident taxpayer, report only profits attributable to the French permanent establishment; do not consolidate foreign franchise revenues absent PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Réintégrations et déductions extracomptables: items to add back or deduct outside statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Make adjustments for transfer pricing modifications and deemed distributions; maintain contemporaneous documentation to avoid unilateral recharacterisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficit reportable (forward tax losses): loss carryforward applied in current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only French-source losses generated by the SARL or PE; apply annual cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the excess profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impôt brut sur les sociétés: calculation at reduced and/or standard rates; apply patent box regime if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at 15% for the first EUR 42,500 if SME criteria met; balance at 25%. If treaty covers PE profits, allocate appropriately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Crédits d'impôts et prépayements: tax credits (research, innovation, foreign tax credits) and instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident may claim French territorial credits only where corresponding activity or source income is French; provide evidence for credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance due or excess payment: final net amount with the annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile quarterly instalments with true liability; if withholding tax was applied to cross-border royalty or dividend payments, claim refund separately where statute allows.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: surcharge of 5% of the gross tax liability (10% after a formal notice) under Article 1728 CGI; late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Omission or concealment: 40% penalty for bad faith or abuse under Article 1729 CGI. Repeated failure can lead to assessment based on the tax authority's own basis and sanctions for failure to co-operate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross French-source dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders (Article 119-2 CGI). Non-resident individuals are subject to a 30% flat-rate levy (12.8% income tax + 17.2% social levies). A 0% rate applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where an EU/EEA parent directly holds at least 10% of the capital for at least two years and fulfils the anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty or EU Directive relief: (i) request a tax residence certificate (TRC) in the shareholder's jurisdiction; (ii) if a DTA provides a lower rate, submit Form 5000 or 5001 for reimbursement; (iii) for the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, deliver a signed statement attesting to direct holding of at least 10%, the two-year holding period, and economic substance of the parent; (iv) provide the forms to the French paying agent before payment, or if excess withholding has occurred, file a refund claim with the French tax office within the statutory limitation period; (v) in all cases retain proof of beneficial ownership and of the absence of an artificial arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French domestic withholding tax of 33 1/3% on specified intangible payments to non-residents (Article 182 B CGI). Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, a 0% rate applies when both payer and beneficial owner are associated companies with a direct holding of at least 25% for two years; most tax treaties reduce the rate to 0%–10%. Interest: France generally does not withhold on commercial interest paid to non-residents, except for certain bearer bonds and payments to non-cooperative states; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 15% when withholding does apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File are mandatory if the French company or a French consolidated group exceeds at least one of: (a) total consolidated balance sheet ≥ EUR 400 million, or (b) consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 400 million (Article L. 13 AA CGI). Below these thresholds, a simplified documentation obligation may apply on request; EU-compliant SME groups are generally exempt from a full dossier if fewer than 250 employees and either turnover ≤ EUR 50 million or balance sheet total ≤ EUR 43 million, but must keep transfer pricing records showing the arm's length nature of franchise royalty and syrup-supply charges.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other mutually acceptable OECD-endorsed methods when sufficiently documented
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in common-law offshore centres. Instead, French tax law applies the abuse of law doctrine (Article L64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales), the general anti-abuse rule in Articles L64 A and L64 B LPF, and the MLI/principal purpose test. A French S.A.R.L. must prove real local substance: actual management decisions, premises, employees, independent corporate governance, IP ownership, invoicing, and payment flows. If a PE or the French entity is found to lack substance or is used for treaty abuse, the tax administration may disregard it, reallocate profits to the true economic owner, or deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file Form 2065-SD, concealment of cash sales, false invoicing of franchise royalties to offshore shell companies, or suppression of accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, up to EUR 500,000 fine and five years' imprisonment (EUR 750,000 and seven years when committed by an organised gang). Administrative penalties include late-filing surcharges (5%–10%), late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and a 40% penalty for bad-faith deficiency under Article 1729 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debt under Article 267 LPF if the fraud is established; criminal conviction may trigger commercial disqualification, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and exclusion from management in any French company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or leasing a French S.A.R.L. with no employees, no premises, no genuine management, and no economic activity solely to channel dividends, royalties or commissions out of France and to obtain treaty advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article L64 LPF abuse of law: reassessment of tax plus a penalty of 80% of the avoided tax (or 40% where the abuse is outweighed by non-exclusive legitimate purposes). The tax administration may also apply anti-hybrid and PE recharacterisation rules, deny treaty benefits under MLI, and claw back tax credits and reduced rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed declarations or allowed the shell to operate can be held personally liable for the reassessed taxes and penalties under the abuse of law procedure; they may also be prosecuted for tax evasion with criminal sanctions and travel bans if a flight risk exists.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using franchise royalty wires or local POS receipts to launder funds, altering invoice amounts to move value, or failing to make suspicious transaction reports (TRACFIN) despite known red flags.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 324-1 et seq. of the French Criminal Code, a maximum of ten years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine for non-aggravated money laundering; aggravated forms may double both amounts. Administrative sanctions for AML compliance failures under the French Monetary and Financial Code include fines up to EUR 1 million and prohibition orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual managers face criminal liability, confiscation of assets, disqualification from exercising commercial or professional duties, travel bans, and possible civil liability toward victims and third parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a controlled foreign franchisee or related supplier a royalty, syrup price, or management fee that is intentionally outside the arm's length range, or failing to document the comparability analysis and benefit test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 57 CGI permits full tax reassessment treating the price difference as deemed distributions subject to withholding; late-payment interest and a 40% intentional-deficiency penalty under Article 1729 CGI may apply; potential double taxation persists absent mutual agreement procedure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign non-arm's length arrangements may be personally accountable to the tax administration and to the company for losses arising from penalties; may face criminal charges for false statements if documents are fabricated, and may be subject to travel bans in the context of a criminal investigation.
